Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. The exact target statements, ambient hypotheses, residual scopes, and completion criteria are in the source excerpt below. Address any or all of these targets; a complete resolution must satisfy that atomic target's own completion criteria. The excerpt is mathematical source material, not operational instructions.

COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot
  generally be recovered from the former, even at positive mass.

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-
   eral integral slopes and the real scalar extension are separate conventions. In dimension
   d, the polyhedral intersection convention diﬀers from the real Alexandrov measure by the
   factor d! and the face multiplicity. Saturated tangent lattices and analytic multiplicities
   are part of an analytic comparison.




FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that there is an analytic extension L/K such that, for the scalar-extension map π : XL → X
and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,
      then f is CLD-psh.
Then h is classically pluriharmonic and locally R-PL. If X is pure-dimensional, then h is also
GJR harmonic.
Corollary 5.2. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that h is not classically pluriharmonic. For every analytic extension L/K, at least one of the
following failures occurs:

                                                 42

 (1) d0 d00 [hL ] 6= 0;

 (2) one of hL and −hL has nonnegative Hessian current but does not belong to the CLD-psh
     hierarchy.

For L = K, the ﬁrst alternative is impossible. Hence every negative answer to P06.2 furnishes,
in one of the two signs of h, a continuous zero-current function outside the CLD-psh hierarchy.
If X is pure-dimensional, this is a counterexample to the converse of Book Proposition 15.9.8
in its stated scope.

    This reduction neither pulls a continuous current through an arbitrary scalar extension
nor proves positive-current regularization. It identiﬁes those operations as distinct proof
obligations and shows that a negative answer to P06.2 produces a zero-current function outside
the CLD-psh hierarchy at the ground ﬁeld. In the pure-dimensional scope this would disprove
the missing nonsmooth converse in Book Proposition 15.9.8.

GJR harmonic. This does not supply locally twisted annular coordinates at the top or insert
annular stages at arbitrary intermediate levels of the tower.
     Annular geometry may also occur at the bottom. The general transfer statement Book
Proposition M.1.34 isolates the common exact descent, classical-pluriharmonic transfer, R-
harmonic transfer, and ﬁrst-current-rigidity transfer of the four allowed bundle types over an
arbitrary admissible base. Applying it to a globally coordinated curve-polyannulus product
gives Book Corollary M.1.53: after any such mixed tower, the top function still has the
unique logarithmic coeﬃcient formula over the original curve. Applying it instead to a locally
trivial curve-polyannulus bundle or a locally trivial mixed curve-polycylinder bundle gives
Book Corollary M.1.54, Book Corollary M.1.55, with classical pluriharmonicity, local R-PL
regularity, and GJR harmonicity but no global coeﬃcient formula. Thus locally twisted
annular coordinates are now allowed at the bottom of the mixed exact tower. The result
still requires their displayed analytic local trivializations and does not allow an annular stage
to be interleaved at an arbitrary later level, an annular ﬁbration without such charts, or an
arbitrary nonproduct germ.

In Book Theorem M.1.20, each stage of a ﬁnite boundaryless tower over the curve may be
either one of the four exact bundle types or a globally coordinated ﬁnite standard strict
open-polyannulus product. An induction preserves classical pluriharmonicity, R-harmonicity,
and ﬁrst-current rigidity at every level. It gives a unique normal form on the tower top
with one logarithmic term for every annular coordinate introduced anywhere in the tower;
the zero-current base coeﬃcient and all locally constant slope coeﬃcients live on the original
curve. Thus globally coordinated annular stages may now occur at arbitrary levels. For a
global normal form, the remaining obstruction is the transition monodromy of locally twisted
annulus bundles: the theorem does not choose global annular coordinates. For one locally
trivial polyannulus bundle over the curve, however, Book Proposition M.1.26 now identiﬁes the
coeﬃcient system on overlaps. The logarithmic coordinates transform by a locally constant
unimodular integer matrix and a vector of zero-current base functions. These data satisfy
the aﬃne cocycle law, deﬁne a rank-s local system of lattices, and make the local slope
vectors of every zero-current function a global parallel section of its dual real local system.
Thus the monodromy defect is encoded intrinsically even when it is not trivialized. The
remaining translation defect is measured exactly by the zero-current radiance class of Book
Deﬁnition M.1.1. Book Proposition M.1.27 makes its vanishing equivalent to a purely linear
overlap law after zero-current aﬃne gauge and then gives one global coeﬃcient formula for

does not vanish, Book Proposition M.1.28 gives the exact residual answer slope by slope: the
slopes of global zero-current functions are precisely the parallel dual sections whose scalar

every zero-current function to the original curve. When the radiance class vanishes, a chosen

deliberately gives no global coeﬃcient formula. It also does not treat annular trivializations

Investigate the following open-problem family in non-Archimedean pluripotential theory. Active atomic targets: P06.2. COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where
   a statement requires them. X an is Berkovich analytiﬁcation. “Ordinary open” refers
   to its ordinary topology, rather than an admissible G-cover. A statement on one ﬁxed
   polycylinder is weaker than an every-open statement obtained from an actual basis.

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not
  an identiﬁcation of all normalizers. The symbol X ℶ denotes the valuative/trivially valued
  carrier used by the raw ideal transform.

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot

Polyhedral normalization.

Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose

clusion for noninvariant functions, nonsplit forms, annular ﬁbres, or arbitrary disc ﬁbrations.
The same conclusion persists through every ﬁnite tower of such bundles when the maximal
compact torus acts on every level and all bundle maps are equivariant: successive exact
descents preserve invariance and reduce to the same split-toric base theorem; see Book Corol-
lary M.1.64. The same bundle scope descends through a chosen complete extension that is the
completion of an algebraic extension when the base becomes the displayed split toric domain
and all three of the lifted action, invariance, and zero-current conditions hold upstairs; see
Book Corollary M.1.68. The corresponding ﬁnite-tower statement is Book Corollary M.1.69;
it requires the full compatible tower, action, invariance, and current equation after that chosen
extension. It does not manufacture the extension or bundle chart, and supplies no automatic
ascent of a downstairs current equality. Its analytic-local form Book Corollary M.1.70 requires
that displayed structure only near each point of the total space; it makes no assertion when
such neighbourhood data are absent. The same localisation is valid for ﬁnite towers: Book
Corollary M.1.71 requires a complete displayed tower near each point of the total space, with
the scalar-stable extension, the compatible action on every level, and equivariance of every
map. It supplies the same three conclusions locally, but does not create that tower or transfer
a downstairs current equation upstairs.
     The former third atom in this environment is now resolved. Book Theorem 19.3.4 proves
that every continuous current-psh function on every smooth proper algebraic curve over an
algebraically closed complete nontrivially valued ﬁeld is, locally on a strict aﬃnoid neigh-
bourhood, a uniformly convergent decreasing sequence of ordinary CLD-smooth psh func-
tions. Equivalently, current positivity, Thuillier subharmonicity, and the ﬁrst ordinary-smooth

decreasing-limit stage coincide in this scope. The proof passes through ﬁnite local tree skeleta,
rational strictiﬁcation of graph Laplacians, Riemann–Roch movement of residual divisors into

    The formerly written harmonic-approximant strengthening is false: Book Proposi-
tion 19.3.2 constructs an integral PL weakly smooth harmonic function on a smooth proper
curve which is not even a locally uniform limit of ordinary CLD-smooth harmonic functions.
Its ﬁxed-support argument uses zero curvature of every approximant and says nothing against
the now-proved psh regularization theorem, whose approximants carry positive curvature
in fresh directions. The exact-live proposition and proof passed production Rethlas run
20260825T055907Z_b5c8f0719b60, item pi_d80993bb01a748f0422ae6a5, with the same
model and scrutiny, ﬁnal correct, zero critical errors, and zero gaps. Thus weakly smooth
and CLD-smooth harmonic regularity on curves are genuinely diﬀerent. The supplied proof
in Book Section 18.12 now covers all singular points under the original P06.1 hypotheses,
beyond the preceding product, quotient and toroidal cases. It uses closed-subspace PL germs,
ﬁnite and proper descent, regular alteration covers and completed-algebraic scalar descent.
Its provenance is the author-supplied manuscript, separately recorded from the historical

notes.summary: Unverified proof of exact finite-stage descent of every compact ordinary CLD smooth scalar test under completion of an algebraic extension. The argument descends rational domains, strict ordinary neighbourhoods, unit norms and compact supports; coefficient density alone is not assumed sufficient.
notes.detailedSummary: Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, M/K an algebraic valued extension, L its completion, and X good and separated. Every compactly supported ordinary CLD smooth scalar function on X_L is the exact pullback of a compactly supported ordinary smooth scalar function on X_E for some finite K-subfield E of M. A positive weighted lower bound for a rational denominator/numerator system makes sufficiently close finite-stage approximants preserve both its weak and strict conjunctions, including equality walls and zero coordinates. Unit approximants preserve norms exactly on compact rational domains. A finite compact partition at a common finite stage gives global descent without assuming saturation of the original support or compatibility of separate downstairs descriptions. Finite-stage tensor associativity, scalar surjectivity and compact inverse images are proved. This is a test-descent theorem, not recognition or an arbitrary-current pullback theorem.
notes.text:
This note records an unverified mathematical proof draft. The authoritative argument is P06.2-argument.md, particularly Sections 2.1 and 12, with the standalone P06.2-partial.tex and P06.2-partial.pdf. All new artifacts are in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-11/P06.2-completed-algebraic-curve-continuation/artifacts/codex-Ntn6OZ. Rerun python3 prepare-sources.py, python3 append-primary.py, and python3 build-and-check.py there. No earlier draft theorem, review or native note is a premise.

Exact statement. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, M/K an algebraic extension with its extending absolute value, L=completion(M), and X a good separated K-analytic space. Write q_E:X_L→X_E for scalar projection to a finite K-subfield E of M. For every β∈A_c^{0,0}(X_L), where A denotes ordinary CLD smooth forms, there exist E and α∈A_c^{0,0}(X_E) such that β=q_E*α exactly as ordinary smooth scalar sections. Consequently d'd''β=q_E*(d'd''α). No pure dimension, boundarylessness, strictness, global quasicompactness or global paracompactness is needed for this subsidiary statement.

Analytic foundations used. In the inspected CLD snapshot, arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, Sections 11.1.1–2 give compact Hausdorff affinoid spectra, their evaluation topology, noetherian affinoid algebras with closed ideals, and spectral surjectivity onto prime ideals. Sections 11.1.5 and 11.1.7–9 give rational analytic domains, good affinoid neighbourhood bases, ordinary opens as analytic domains, analytic sheaf restriction, scalar extension by completed tensors and inverse images of analytic domains. Rational systems have positive real radii and denominator/numerators with no common zero. The neighbourhood clause provides a rational domain inside a prescribed ordinary open with the chosen point satisfying every associated strict inequality. CLD15.1.2 supplies ordinary local scalar descriptions φ(−log|f_1|,…,−log|f_m|) by analytic units and smooth Euclidean coefficients. CLD3.4.6 identifies scalar sections with numerical functions; its proof uses compact moment nullity, CLD3.4.1 and 3.4.4. CLD3.3.12 and 6.2.2 give ordinary smooth differential functoriality and sheaf operations. Exact used statements and available primary proof bodies are included in Section 15 of the authoritative argument. The new domain and support lemmas are proved below, rather than attributed to a density slogan.

Finite fields and tensors. Every finite valued extension E/K is complete, and its norm is equivalent to a coordinate maximum norm. To prove this, induct on dimension: the preceding basis span is complete and hence closed, so the last basis vector has positive distance from that span. This bounds its coefficient, and the ultrametric inequality bounds the others. Coordinate functionals are therefore bounded. Tensoring them with a complete affinoid A shows A completed-tensor_K E=A tensor_K E, with the finite-module topology, including nilpotents. Finite extending absolute values are unique: norm equivalence applied to powers of an element, followed by taking roots, eliminates the comparison constants. Existence follows from the nonempty analytic spectrum of a finite field algebra with its finite-module Banach topology, using CLD11.4.4.

The image of A tensor_K M is dense in A_L. First approximate by a finite tensor with L coefficients; then approximate those coefficients in M. The tensor error is bounded by max_j ||a_j||·|λ_j−m_j|. This concerns the image and assumes neither isometry nor injectivity of the infinite uncompleted tensor. A finite list of coefficients lies in one finite subfield because M/K is algebraic and its finite subfields form a directed union. M itself is never treated as a complete analytic field.

For a finite E/K, the maps (a⊗e)⊗λ↦a⊗eλ and a⊗λ↦(a⊗1)⊗λ give inverse bounded maps (A_E) completed-tensor_E L≅A completed-tensor_K L. Boundedness of the first uses the finite coordinate functionals of E; boundedness of the second uses the tensor inequality. They are inverse on dense elementary tensors and hence on completions. This proves exactly the finite-stage associativity used in the analytic identifications, including for arbitrary-radius affinoid algebras.

Scalar surjectivity in this scope has a direct proof. For x∈M(A), put H=H(x). Embed the algebraic field M into an algebraic closure of H over K, by extending partial embeddings through roots of minimal polynomials. The unique norms on finite extensions of complete H are compatible. Their restriction to every finite K-subfield of M is the prescribed norm by uniqueness. Complete that algebraic closure to a field F; the isometric embedding M→F extends to L→F. Evaluation A⊗_K L→F satisfies |Σ a_j(x)λ_j|≤max_j||a_j||·|λ_j| for every representation with L coefficients. Taking the infimum bounds it by the full tensor seminorm, so it extends through the separated completion and supplies a point over x. The same argument over E proves surjectivity to each finite-stage affinoid, including rational domains. It does not bound only M-coefficient representations or assume tensor-norm compatibility.

Inverse images of compact sets under these projections are compact. Cover a compact set by finitely many ordinary interiors of affinoid neighbourhoods. Its inverse image is closed in the finite union of their compact scalar extensions, since the carriers are Hausdorff. No finite-fibre assertion is involved.

Exact rational-system lemma. Suppose B=A completed-tensor_{E_0} L and a rational domain R_L⊂M(B) has system |f_i|≤r_i|g|, with r_i>0 and no common zero. Define δ=min_y max(|g(y)|, |f_1(y)|/r_1,…,|f_s(y)|/r_s)>0. Choose g′,f_i′ at one finite stage E⊃E_0 with Banach errors less than δ·min(1,r_1,…,r_s). Every evaluation then satisfies |g′−g|<δ and |f_i′−f_i|<r_iδ.

Both the weak conjunction and the strict conjunction are unchanged. If |g(y)|≥δ, its norm is unchanged. For each numerator at least r_i|g(y)| its norm is unchanged; for each smaller numerator its perturbed norm remains strictly smaller than r_i|g′(y)|. Thus all weak comparisons and equality walls are preserved. If |g(y)|<δ, some numerator has |f_i(y)|/r_i≥δ. That numerator retains its norm, while |g′(y)|<δ, so a strict violation persists. This also covers g(y)=0 and zero numerators. No zero coefficient is logarithmed and no nilpotent is removed.

The approximated system has no common zero upstairs, hence none at the finite stage by surjectivity. Its elements generate the unit ideal: otherwise a maximal ideal containing them would give an analytic common zero. It therefore defines an actual rational domain R_E. Its scalar extension has exactly the original validity locus. Uniqueness of analytic domain structure, by the analytic-domain factorization property in CLD11.1.7, identifies it with R_L without reduction. The strict locus O_E is ordinary open, and q_E^{-1}(O_E) is exactly the original strict locus. Real radii remain unchanged; there is no assertion that absolute analytic interiors commute with extension.

The strong rational-neighbourhood clause can also be seen directly. The affinoid topology is initial for evaluations. Inside a prescribed open choose finitely many tighter bounds |a_j|>ℓ_j>0 and |b_k|<u_k. Put g=product_j a_j, or g=1 when there are no lower bounds. Choose C with C^{-1}<product_j ℓ_j. The system |1|≤C|g|, |product_{j′≠j}a_{j′}|≤ℓ_j^{-1}|g|, and |b_kg|≤u_k|g| is rational, has no common zero because one numerator is 1, lies inside the original open and is strict at the chosen point. Thus exact rational-system descent supplies a finite-stage ordinary neighbourhood of each selected point, without trying to control an entire infinite fibre.

Local scalar descent. Near y∈X_L write β=φ(t_{f_1},…,t_{f_m}) on an ordinary open, where t_f=−log|f|. Choose a downstairs affinoid neighbourhood V_0 and an ordinary open U_0 in its interior containing the image of y. In V_{0,L}, choose a rational neighbourhood R_L of y inside both U_{0,L} and the scalar-description open, with y in its strict locus. Descend it as above. Surjectivity shows R_E lies in U_{0,E}, so its strict locus is an ordinary open of the entire X_E.

On compact R_L each unit f_j has positive minimum norm δ_j. Approximate it in the actual rational affinoid algebra by u_j at a common finite stage, with Banach error <δ_j. Ultrametricity gives |u_j|=|f_j| everywhere on R_L. Surjectivity and the maximal-ideal unit criterion show u_j is an actual unit on R_E, with its inverse in that algebra. The downstairs moment image equals the upstairs one, so the same Euclidean coefficient φ is defined there. The ordinary function b_E=φ(t_{u_1},…,t_{u_m}) pulls back exactly to β on the descended strict open. Numerical equality is equality of scalar sections by CLD3.4.6; differentiation therefore respects it. This is not an inference of C2 convergence from C0 approximation.

Compact partitions used here are only the finite compact-cover specialization of CLD15.2.5. A direct bump construction is supplied in Section 2.1: choose a rational neighbourhood inside the desired open, with strict numerator bounds at the point. A smooth cutoff in log|g| excludes small denominator norm. Smooth cutoffs in log|f_i/g| exclude ratios near the rational boundary, and extend as the constant one near numerator zeros. Their product has compact support strictly inside the rational neighbourhood, so it extends smoothly by zero to the ambient space. Finite sums and a real smooth composition give a bump equal to one near a compact set. For a finite cover, choose nonnegative point bumps ψ_i whose positive loci cover the compact set, set s=Σψ_i, choose χ=1 near that set supported in {s>0}, and put θ_i=χψ_i/s there, extended by zero. Each θ_i is compactly supported in its cover member and Σθ_i=1 near the compact set. The broad countable-at-infinity fixed-index compact-support claim is unused.

Global compact test. Cover F=supp β by finitely many descended description opens, and enlarge to a common finite field E. Write O_{i,L}=q_E^{-1}(O_{i,E}) and β=q_E*b_{i,E} there. The compact image F_E=q_E(F) is covered by the O_{i,E}. Choose the preceding compact partition θ_i at this finite stage and define α=Σ_i extension-by-zero(θ_i b_{i,E}). Each product has compact support inside its ordinary open, so every exterior point has a zero neighbourhood and the extension is ordinary smooth. Globally q_E*α=(Σ_i θ_i∘q_E)β=β: the sum is one on F, while β is zero outside F. No saturation of F or prior agreement of the b_i on downstairs overlaps is assumed. The resulting α has compact support, its full inverse image is compact, and its smooth Hessian pulls back exactly.

Limitations. This theorem is descent of scalar tests to some finite stage, not descent of analytic functions themselves, arbitrary-current pullback, or a recognition theorem. The proof is fallible and has no independent verification. The authoritative file includes the primary bodies and the full argument; successful diagnostics do not establish its mathematical correctness.

Finite separable and Frobenius dependencies are reconstructed. Original P06.2 recognition remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: For L equal to the completion of any algebraic valued extension M/K, the draft proves D[h]=0 iff D[h∘π]=0 on every good separated strict boundaryless pure one-dimensional X and for every continuous finite h. This includes completed algebraic closures and mixed inseparable/separable extensions. Exact compact test descent from n1 reduces completion to finite algebraic stages. Finite separable ascent is reconstructed by scalar polarization, actual orbit characteristic polynomials, C1 Newton power sums, tangential mollification on collision-contained segments, calibrated carrier total variation and two correctly ordered fixed-support limits. Finite purely inseparable ascent is reconstructed through Frobenius powers and exact scalar-test descent; an embedded separable–purely-inseparable decomposition handles every finite stage. Local purity after completion is checked by descending a hypothetical zero-dimensional rational neighbourhood. Scalar calibrated measure projection has no degree factor. No recognition, two-sign regularization, universal curve-probe transport or higher-dimensional separable-current ascent is claimed.
notes.text:
Claimed theorem, unverified draft. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, M/K an algebraic valued extension and L=completion(M). Let X be good, separated, strict, boundaryless and pure of analytic dimension one, with its actual potentially singular and nonreduced structure. For every continuous finite h:X→R and scalar projection π:X_L→X, the draft proves d'd''[h]=0 iff d'd''[h∘π]=0. It applies on every ordinary open subspace. In particular L may be the completion of an algebraic closure. The forward implication imposes no upstairs current equality, invariance, regularization, product or algebraic-model hypothesis.

The complete argument is P06.2-argument.md, with P06.2-partial.tex and P06.2-partial.pdf in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-11/P06.2-completed-algebraic-curve-continuation/artifacts/codex-Ntn6OZ. Sections 3–10 reconstruct the supplied finite separable proof; Section 11 reconstructs the finite inseparable mechanism and proves the actual mixed-field decomposition; Section 12 contains n1; Section 13 proves the completed implication. Primary statements and available proof bodies are included in Section 15. No earlier theorem, review, publication receipt or native note is assumed. Rerun python3 prepare-sources.py, python3 append-primary.py and python3 build-and-check.py.

Current and calibrated integration conventions. Put D=d'd'' and B_h(ψ)=∫_X h(Dψ)_Rad,K for ψ∈A_c^{0,0}(X). By CLD7.3.5 and smooth current duality, D[h]=0 is exactly vanishing of all these pairings, up to a harmless fixed duality sign. D[h] itself is not assumed to be a measure. CLD15.7.1–2 applies to topologically separated pure-dimensional spaces and supplies the canonical calibrated tropical structure, compatible with domains. All differentiated smooth top forms define finite signed Radon measures on compact supports.

The inspected sources are CLD, arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, and GR, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025. GR2.11(5′) states ∂(Y_L/Z_L)⊂π^{-1}∂(Y/Z), so boundarylessness persists; its domain-interior and composition statements 2.11(3),(4) give ordinary-open localization. Goodness comes from inverse images of affinoid neighbourhoods; strictness from strict presentations; separatedness from base change of the diagonal. CLD11.2.3 preserves total analytic dimension under complete scalar extension and local dimension under domains. Local purity is checked separately below.

Canonical measures and the indispensable projection identity. CLD14.3.2–5 constructs positive standard calibrations on convenient skeletal cells. With a torus projection injective on a top cell, its volume vector is the inverse affine projection of the standard volume vector multiplied by the actual finite-flat degree. These degrees are fibre-algebra dimensions, retaining nilpotent lengths. CLD5.8.3–5 contracts top forms on supporting skeletons to volume forms and Radon measures. CLD5.10.1 gives calibrated integration on pleasant compact moment charts. Compact moment images are finite polyhedra; only this assertion of CLD12.2.4 is used. The dimension upper bound is separately CLD12.2.10: dim_trop,x f≤d_K(x)≤dim_x X, and compact image dimension is their supremum. Thus curve images have dimension at most one. No universal equality between moment-image and source dimension is assumed.

CLD14.3.6 and 15.3.1 state, for any complete scalar extension and locally integrable top G-form ω, π_*ω_L,Rad=ω_Rad. Their proof compares convenient skeletal cells. For a chosen upstairs target Gauss lift, CLD13.3.3 gives the downstairs local moment degree as the sum of upstairs local degrees. On the zero-dimensional fibre this is simply the dimension of an Artinian algebra after tensoring and decomposing into its local factors; the dimensions sum to the original dimension over the extended field. The calibrated volume vectors therefore sum correctly. Contracting the pulled-back form gives the Radon identity. It has no field-degree factor, even for infinite extensions, and is applied here only to smooth differentiated top forms.

Finite restriction of the same carrier is different. CLD14.4.3 states μ_Z0=[E:K]μ_Z for an E-analytic level-one space regarded on the same carrier as K-analytic. Its proof uses the finite-flat scalar projection of the split torus. An actual analytic isomorphism preserves the restricted K-calibration and measures: the convenient-cell fibre algebras are isomorphic and their degrees agree; this is also the isomorphism case of CLD15.4.3. Cancelling the same-carrier factor proves invariance of the E-calibrated measures under the semilinear finite Galois action. No factor is transferred to scalar projection.

Reconstructed finite separable ascent. First suppose E/K is finite Galois with group G and d=|G|. The finite tensor proof in n1 gives B=A⊗_K E. Tensoring the kernel of z↦(gz−z)_g proves B^G=A without division in K. Invariant units descend with their invariant inverses. A fibre is M(H(x)⊗_K E), a finite product of fields because a separable primitive polynomial factors without repetitions. Each field has its unique extending norm and one analytic point. boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose

GJR harmonic.

notes.summary: Unverified proof of exact finite-stage descent of every compact ordinary CLD smooth scalar test under completion of an algebraic extension. The argument descends rational domains, strict ordinary neighbourhoods, unit norms and compact supports; coefficient density alone is not assumed sufficient.
notes.detailedSummary: Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, M/K an algebraic valued extension, L its completion, and X good and separated. Every compactly supported ordinary CLD smooth scalar function on X_L is the exact pullback of a compactly supported ordinary smooth scalar function on X_E for some finite K-subfield E of M. A positive weighted lower bound for a rational denominator/numerator system makes sufficiently close finite-stage approximants preserve both its weak and strict conjunctions, including equality walls and zero coordinates. Unit approximants preserve norms exactly on compact rational domains. A finite compact partition at a common finite stage gives global descent without assuming saturation of the original support or compatibility of separate downstairs descriptions. Finite-stage tensor associativity, scalar surjectivity and compact inverse images are proved. This is a test-descent theorem, not recognition or an arbitrary-current pullback theorem.
notes.text:
This note records an unverified mathematical proof draft. The authoritative argument is P06.2-argument.md, particularly Sections 2.1 and 12, with the standalone P06.2-partial.tex and P06.2-partial.pdf. All new artifacts are in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-11/P06.2-completed-algebraic-curve-continuation/artifacts/codex-Ntn6OZ. Rerun python3 prepare-sources.py, python3 append-primary.py, and python3 build-and-check.py there. No earlier draft theorem, review or native note is a premise.

Exact statement. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, M/K an algebraic extension with its extending absolute value, L=completion(M), and X a good separated K-analytic space. Write q_E:X_L→X_E for scalar projection to a finite K-subfield E of M. For every β∈A_c^{0,0}(X_L), where A denotes ordinary CLD smooth forms, there exist E and α∈A_c^{0,0}(X_E) such that β=q_E*α exactly as ordinary smooth scalar sections. Consequently d'd''β=q_E*(d'd''α). No pure dimension, boundarylessness, strictness, global quasicompactness or global paracompactness is needed for this subsidiary statement.

Analytic foundations used. In the inspected CLD snapshot, arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, Sections 11.1.1–2 give compact Hausdorff affinoid spectra, their evaluation topology, noetherian affinoid algebras with closed ideals, and spectral surjectivity onto prime ideals. Sections 11.1.5 and 11.1.7–9 give rational analytic domains, good affinoid neighbourhood bases, ordinary opens as analytic domains, analytic sheaf restriction, scalar extension by completed tensors and inverse images of analytic domains. Rational systems have positive real radii and denominator/numerators with no common zero. The neighbourhood clause provides a rational domain inside a prescribed ordinary open with the chosen point satisfying every associated strict inequality. CLD15.1.2 supplies ordinary local scalar descriptions φ(−log|f_1|,…,−log|f_m|) by analytic units and smooth Euclidean coefficients. CLD3.4.6 identifies scalar sections with numerical functions; its proof uses compact moment nullity, CLD3.4.1 and 3.4.4. CLD3.3.12 and 6.2.2 give ordinary smooth differential functoriality and sheaf operations. Exact used statements and available primary proof bodies are included in Section 15 of the authoritative argument. The new domain and support lemmas are proved below, rather than attributed to a density slogan.

Finite fields and tensors. Every finite valued extension E/K is complete, and its norm is equivalent to a coordinate maximum norm. To prove this, induct on dimension: the preceding basis span is complete and hence closed, so the last basis vector has positive distance from that span. This bounds its coefficient, and the ultrametric inequality bounds the others. Coordinate functionals are therefore bounded. Tensoring them with a complete affinoid A shows A completed-tensor_K E=A tensor_K E, with the finite-module topology, including nilpotents. Finite extending absolute values are unique: norm equivalence applied to powers of an element, followed by taking roots, eliminates the comparison constants. Existence follows from the nonempty analytic spectrum of a finite field algebra with its finite-module Banach topology, using CLD11.4.4.

The image of A tensor_K M is dense in A_L. First approximate by a finite tensor with L coefficients; then approximate those coefficients in M. The tensor error is bounded by max_j ||a_j||·|λ_j−m_j|. This concerns the image and assumes neither isometry nor injectivity of the infinite uncompleted tensor. A finite list of coefficients lies in one finite subfield because M/K is algebraic and its finite subfields form a directed union. M itself is never treated as a complete analytic field.

For a finite E/K, the maps (a⊗e)⊗λ↦a⊗eλ and a⊗λ↦(a⊗1)⊗λ give inverse bounded maps (A_E) completed-tensor_E L≅A completed-tensor_K L. Boundedness of the first uses the finite coordinate functionals of E; boundedness of the second uses the tensor inequality. They are inverse on dense elementary tensors and hence on completions. This proves exactly the finite-stage associativity used in the analytic identifications, including for arbitrary-radius affinoid algebras.

Scalar surjectivity in this scope has a direct proof. For x∈M(A), put H=H(x). Embed the algebraic field M into an algebraic closure of H over K, by extending partial embeddings through roots of minimal polynomials. The unique norms on finite extensions of complete H are compatible. Their restriction to every finite K-subfield of M is the prescribed norm by uniqueness. Complete that algebraic closure to a field F; the isometric embedding M→F extends to L→F. Evaluation A⊗_K L→F satisfies |Σ a_j(x)λ_j|≤max_j||a_j||·|λ_j| for every representation with L coefficients. Taking the infimum bounds it by the full tensor seminorm, so it extends through the separated completion and supplies a point over x. The same argument over E proves surjectivity to each finite-stage affinoid, including rational domains. It does not bound only M-coefficient representations or assume tensor-norm compatibility.

Inverse images of compact sets under these projections are compact. Cover a compact set by finitely many ordinary interiors of affinoid neighbourhoods. Its inverse image is closed in the finite union of their compact scalar extensions, since the carriers are Hausdorff. No finite-fibre assertion is involved.

Exact rational-system lemma. Suppose B=A completed-tensor_{E_0} L and a rational domain R_L⊂M(B) has system |f_i|≤r_i|g|, with r_i>0 and no common zero. Define δ=min_y max(|g(y)|, |f_1(y)|/r_1,…,|f_s(y)|/r_s)>0. Choose g′,f_i′ at one finite stage E⊃E_0 with Banach errors less than δ·min(1,r_1,…,r_s). Every evaluation then satisfies |g′−g|<δ and |f_i′−f_i|<r_iδ.

Both the weak conjunction and the strict conjunction are unchanged. If |g(y)|≥δ, its norm is unchanged. For each numerator at least r_i|g(y)| its norm is unchanged; for each smaller numerator its perturbed norm remains strictly smaller than r_i|g′(y)|. Thus all weak comparisons and equality walls are preserved. If |g(y)|<δ, some numerator has |f_i(y)|/r_i≥δ. That numerator retains its norm, while |g′(y)|<δ, so a strict violation persists. This also covers g(y)=0 and zero numerators. No zero coefficient is logarithmed and no nilpotent is removed.

The approximated system has no common zero upstairs, hence none at the finite stage by surjectivity. Its elements generate the unit ideal: otherwise a maximal ideal containing them would give an analytic common zero. It therefore defines an actual rational domain R_E. Its scalar extension has exactly the original validity locus. Uniqueness of analytic domain structure, by the analytic-domain factorization property in CLD11.1.7, identifies it with R_L without reduction. The strict locus O_E is ordinary open, and q_E^{-1}(O_E) is exactly the original strict locus. Real radii remain unchanged; there is no assertion that absolute analytic interiors commute with extension.

The strong rational-neighbourhood clause can also be seen directly. The affinoid topology is initial for evaluations. Inside a prescribed open choose finitely many tighter bounds |a_j|>ℓ_j>0 and |b_k|<u_k. Put g=product_j a_j, or g=1 when there are no lower bounds. Choose C with C^{-1}<product_j ℓ_j. The system |1|≤C|g|, |product_{j′≠j}a_{j′}|≤ℓ_j^{-1}|g|, and |b_kg|≤u_k|g| is rational, has no common zero because one numerator is 1, lies inside the original open and is strict at the chosen point. Thus exact rational-system descent supplies a finite-stage ordinary neighbourhood of each selected point, without trying to control an entire infinite fibre.

Local scalar descent. Near y∈X_L write β=φ(t_{f_1},…,t_{f_m}) on an ordinary open, where t_f=−log|f|. Choose a downstairs affinoid neighbourhood V_0 and an ordinary open U_0 in its interior containing the image of y. In V_{0,L}, choose a rational neighbourhood R_L of y inside both U_{0,L} and the scalar-description open, with y in its strict locus. Descend it as above. Surjectivity shows R_E lies in U_{0,E}, so its strict locus is an ordinary open of the entire X_E.

On compact R_L each unit f_j has positive minimum norm δ_j. Approximate it in the actual rational affinoid algebra by u_j at a common finite stage, with Banach error <δ_j. Ultrametricity gives |u_j|=|f_j| everywhere on R_L. Surjectivity and the maximal-ideal unit criterion show u_j is an actual unit on R_E, with its inverse in that algebra. The downstairs moment image equals the upstairs one, so the same Euclidean coefficient φ is defined there. The ordinary function b_E=φ(t_{u_1},…,t_{u_m}) pulls back exactly to β on the descended strict open. Numerical equality is equality of scalar sections by CLD3.4.6; differentiation therefore respects it. This is not an inference of C2 convergence from C0 approximation.

Compact partitions used here are only the finite compact-cover specialization of CLD15.2.5. A direct bump construction is supplied in Section 2.1: choose a rational neighbourhood inside the desired open, with strict numerator bounds at the point. A smooth cutoff in log|g| excludes small denominator norm. Smooth cutoffs in log|f_i/g| exclude ratios near the rational boundary, and extend as the constant one near numerator zeros. Their product has compact support strictly inside the rational neighbourhood, so it extends smoothly by zero to the ambient space. Finite sums and a real smooth composition give a bump equal to one near a compact set. For a finite cover, choose nonnegative point bumps ψ_i whose positive loci cover the compact set, set s=Σψ_i, choose χ=1 near that set supported in {s>0}, and put θ_i=χψ_i/s there, extended by zero. Each θ_i is compactly supported in its cover member and Σθ_i=1 near the compact set. The broad countable-at-infinity fixed-index compact-support claim is unused.

Global compact test. Cover F=supp β by finitely many descended description opens, and enlarge to a common finite field E. Write O_{i,L}=q_E^{-1}(O_{i,E}) and β=q_E*b_{i,E} there. The compact image F_E=q_E(F) is covered by the O_{i,E}. Choose the preceding compact partition θ_i at this finite stage and define α=Σ_i extension-by-zero(θ_i b_{i,E}). Each product has compact support inside its ordinary open, so every exterior point has a zero neighbourhood and the extension is ordinary smooth. Globally q_E*α=(Σ_i θ_i∘q_E)β=β: the sum is one on F, while β is zero outside F. No saturation of F or prior agreement of the b_i on downstairs overlaps is assumed. The resulting α has compact support, its full inverse image is compact, and its smooth Hessian pulls back exactly.

Limitations. This theorem is descent of scalar tests to some finite stage, not descent of analytic functions themselves, arbitrary-current pullback, or a recognition theorem. The proof is fallible and has no independent verification. The authoritative file includes the primary bodies and the full argument; successful diagnostics do not establish its mathematical correctness.

Claimed theorem, unverified draft. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, M/K an algebraic valued extension and L=completion(M). Let X be good, separated, strict, boundaryless and pure of analytic dimension one, with its actual potentially singular and nonreduced structure. For every continuous finite h:X→R and scalar projection π:X_L→X, the draft proves d'd''[h]=0 iff d'd''[h∘π]=0. It applies on every ordinary open subspace. In particular L may be the completion of an algebraic closure. The forward implication imposes no upstairs current equality, invariance, regularization, product or algebraic-model hypothesis.

The complete argument is P06.2-argument.md, with P06.2-partial.tex and P06.2-partial.pdf in /workspace/research/campaigns/round-11/P06.2-completed-algebraic-curve-continuation/artifacts/codex-Ntn6OZ. Sections 3–10 reconstruct the supplied finite separable proof; Section 11 reconstructs the finite inseparable mechanism and proves the actual mixed-field decomposition; Section 12 contains n1; Section 13 proves the completed implication. Primary statements and available proof bodies are included in Section 15. No earlier theorem, review, publication receipt or native note is assumed. Current and calibrated integration conventions. Put D=d'd'' and B_h(ψ)=∫_X h(Dψ)_Rad,K for ψ∈A_c^{0,0}(X). By CLD7.3.5 and smooth current duality, D[h]=0 is exactly vanishing of all these pairings, up to a harmless fixed duality sign. D[h] itself is not assumed to be a measure. CLD15.7.1–2 applies to topologically separated pure-dimensional spaces and supplies the canonical calibrated tropical structure, compatible with domains. All differentiated smooth top forms define finite signed Radon measures on compact supports.

The inspected sources are CLD, arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, and GR, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025. GR2.11(5′) states ∂(Y_L/Z_L)⊂π^{-1}∂(Y/Z), so boundarylessness persists; its domain-interior and composition statements 2.11(3),(4) give ordinary-open localization. Goodness comes from inverse images of affinoid neighbourhoods; strictness from strict presentations; separatedness from base change of the diagonal. CLD11.2.3 preserves total analytic dimension under complete scalar extension and local dimension under domains. Local purity is checked separately below.

Canonical measures and the indispensable projection identity. CLD14.3.2–5 constructs positive standard calibrations on convenient skeletal cells. With a torus projection injective on a top cell, its volume vector is the inverse affine projection of the standard volume vector multiplied by the actual finite-flat degree. These degrees are fibre-algebra dimensions, retaining nilpotent lengths. CLD5.8.3–5 contracts top forms on supporting skeletons to volume forms and Radon measures. CLD5.10.1 gives calibrated integration on pleasant compact moment charts. Compact moment images are finite polyhedra; only this assertion of CLD12.2.4 is used. The dimension upper bound is separately CLD12.2.10: dim_trop,x f≤d_K(x)≤dim_x X, and compact image dimension is their supremum. Thus curve images have dimension at most one. No universal equality between moment-image and source dimension is assumed.

CLD14.3.6 and 15.3.1 state, for any complete scalar extension and locally integrable top G-form ω, π_*ω_L,Rad=ω_Rad. Their proof compares convenient skeletal cells. For a chosen upstairs target Gauss lift, CLD13.3.3 gives the downstairs local moment degree as the sum of upstairs local degrees. On the zero-dimensional fibre this is simply the dimension of an Artinian algebra after tensoring and decomposing into its local factors; the dimensions sum to the original dimension over the extended field. The calibrated volume vectors therefore sum correctly. Contracting the pulled-back form gives the Radon identity. It has no field-degree factor, even for infinite extensions, and is applied here only to smooth differentiated top forms.

Tensoring the kernel of z↦(gz−z)_g proves B^G=A without division in K. Invariant units descend with their invariant inverses. A fibre is M(H(x)⊗_K E), a finite product of fields because a separable primitive polynomial factors without repetitions. Each field has its unique extending norm and one analytic point. G acts transitively on these points: two orbits would produce a nontrivial invariant idempotent, contradicting invariants H(x). Stabilizers are allowed; no covering-space assertion follows.

Full-fibre shrinking is valid only at this finite stage. In a downstairs affinoid neighbourhood, the compact complement of an upstairs open containing the entire fibre has closed image excluding x. Shrink to a strict affinoid neighbourhood of x avoiding this image. Its complete inverse image lies in that open. This retains finitely many unit and strict norm conditions simultaneously.

Finite separable purity is checked componentwise. For nilradical J in a strict affinoid A, the injection A/J→product_P Frac(A/P) remains injective after separable tensor. Each fraction-field tensor is a product of fields, so the reduced tensor is reduced and the upstairs nilradical is J⊗E. Kernels of the maps to the field factors have zero intersection; their finite product is zero, forcing each minimal prime upstairs to be one of these kernels. Its contraction is a minimal P downstairs. The injection A/P→B/Q is finite integral, so dimensions agree by lying over, going up and incomparability. These follow respectively from the finite-module determinant argument over a local ring and localization of a finite integral domain over a field to a field. Every component upstairs consequently has dimension one. Reductions are used only for this dimension check, never for measures.

For a compact upstairs scalar test, replace it by its real G-average. The pairing with h∘π is unchanged by the proved measure invariance. Near a full finite fibre, choose disjoint scalar-description opens around its points and shrink until the complete affinoid inverse image lies in their union. Their intersections are compact clopen pieces. Analytic sheaf gluing gives actual idempotents and units equal to each local coordinate on its piece and to one elsewhere. For a∈K× with |a|≠1, the unit e_i+a(1−e_i) has two distinct constant logarithms; a real smooth selector distinguishes the pieces. Hence the invariant scalar test has one smooth Euclidean description Φ(T) on the full inverse image, with a finite tuple of actual units. Adjoin all their translates.

Approximate Φ through order two on a compact box by real polynomials. A proof is to extend with a compact cutoff, convolve with a Gaussian, and approximate the Gaussian convolution and its first two derivatives by Taylor polynomials on the compact difference of the support and box. Uniform continuity of derivatives and Gaussian tail bounds justify the first limit. Real polarization gives z_1…z_k=(1/k!)Σ_{J⊂{1,…,k}}(−1)^{k−|J|}(Σ_{j∈J}z_j)^k. Inclusion-exclusion cancels every term missing a symbol. For unit logarithms, sums are logarithms of product units. Therefore every scalar polynomial's G-average is a finite combination of constants and T_f,k=d^{-1}Σ_g t_gf^k. This preserves mixed orbit correlations; separate symmetric data for the original individual units would not suffice.

For an actual unit f form P_f(Z)=product_g(Z−gf)=Z^d+Σ_{i<d}c_iZ^i. Its coefficients are in A and c_0 is a unit. Each coefficient of Z^{d−k} has valuation at least u_1+…+u_k. At a strict gap u_k<u_{k+1}, the product of the k smallest-valuation roots is the unique dominant summand, so equality holds. Equality also holds for k=0,d. These block-end points give the lower convex hull, including all cancellations and infinite coefficient valuations. A hull segment i<j contributes j−i roots of valuation (v(c_i)−v(c_j))/(j−i).

Carrier domination is proved before signed pushforward. For moment coordinates t_a put ζ=Σ_a d′t_a∧d″t_a with the positive convention. The coefficient C2 polynomial error multiplied by these fixed outer cutoffs has differentiated carrier total variation tending to zero. The multiplier h∘π is bounded on that fixed compact. For every downstairs α_j the smooth scalar projection formula gives B_{h∘π}(π*α_j)=B_h(α_j)=0. Total variation now gives B_{h∘π}(β)=0 for every invariant test and hence, by real averaging, for every test. This proves finite Galois forward ascent. For a finite nongalois separable E/K take its finite Galois normal closure N/K. Its construction is elementary: over infinite K a generic linear combination of two separable generators distinguishes their finitely many embeddings, hence is primitive; adjoining the distinct roots of its separable minimal polynomial gives the finite separable splitting field. Embeddings permute the roots and are automorphisms, and the fixed field is K because embeddings of intermediate simple fields extend. Finite tensor associativity identifies (X_E)_N=X_N. Ascent to N followed by the actual proved reverse calculation for N/E gives ascent to E. This reconstructs the finite separable result rather than importing its pending review.

Finite purely inseparable stages. Let k have characteristic p and F/k be finite purely inseparable with F^q⊂k, q=p^e. In the actual finite tensor, u^q=Σa_i^qλ_i^q∈A. Every upstairs seminorm over x is forced by |u|=|u^q(x)|^{1/q}. Together with scalar surjectivity this makes affinoid projection a homeomorphism, and ordinary affinoid interiors glue it globally. If f is an upstairs unit, f^q=g downstairs is a unit by surjectivity and the analytic zero criterion, and t_f=q^{-1}t_g. Therefore every local ordinary scalar description descends exactly. The compact partition and zero-extension construction produces an exact compact downstairs scalar test for every upstairs test. Smooth differentiation and calibrated projection prove both current directions. Purity is checked using this homeomorphism: a hypothetical upstairs zero-dimensional neighbourhood contains the inverse image of a downstairs affinoid neighbourhood of dimension one, contradicting scalar dimension invariance. Every finite algebraic stage is a genuine composite of these two mechanisms. In characteristic p choose generators a_i of E/K and write each irreducible minimal polynomial as g_i(Z^{p^{e_i}}), repeatedly removing common p factors from its exponents until g_i′≠0. The polynomial g_i is irreducible, since a factorization would lift by substitution, and hence separable. Set S=K(a_i^{p^{e_i}}:i)⊂E. Adjoining separable roots successively gives a finite separable field; the degree-many embeddings argument also verifies intermediate separability. With e=max e_i, every a_i^{p^e} lies in S, and the same holds for every rational expression in the generators. Thus E/S is finite purely inseparable. Characteristic zero already has only separable finite stages.

If local dimension at y were zero, none of its finitely many dimension-one components would contain y. Remove them and choose a rational neighbourhood R_L of y in the remaining ordinary open and within the inverse image of the ordinary interior of V_0, with strict inequalities at y. The component/domain dimension formula gives dim R_L=0. The exact rational-domain lemma of n1 descends R_L to a nonempty domain R_E at a finite stage. X_E is already proved pure one-dimensional, so dim R_E=1, including for non-strict internal chart radii. Scalar dimension invariance gives dim R_L=1, a contradiction. Therefore X_L is pure one-dimensional. Its goodness, strictness, separatedness and boundarylessness were checked above.

Generic lengths are not presumed individually unchanged. Tensoring a composition series of a generic Artinian stalk with the flat upstairs generic stalk shows that length upstairs equals the original length times the generic multiplicity of the base-changed reduction; this is CLD13.2.8 with the structure sheaf. The proof and the Artinian degree-sum proof of calibrated projection retain the actual algebras. No finite extension-degree factor or geometric point count is assigned to an infinite projection.

The reconstructed finite theorem gives D[h_E]=0, where h_E=h∘π_E. Smooth differential functoriality and the E- and L-calibrated measure projection identity give

Compact inverse images make these pairings legitimate for every continuous finite multiplier. Since β was arbitrary, D[h∘π]=0. Conversely, apply the upstairs equation to π*ψ for an arbitrary compact downstairs scalar test ψ and use the same smooth measure identity to get B_h(ψ)=0. It does not solve P06.2, whose target is classical pluriharmonic recognition in arbitrary dimension. Two-sign regularization into the ordinary CLD-psh hierarchy, universal analytic-extension curve probes, normalization transport for recognition and higher-dimensional finite separable differential-form ascent remain unproved. COMMON NOTATION
Common notation and formulation boundaries
Fields and analytic spaces.
   K denotes a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld. Trivial or nontrivial valuation, strictness,
   goodness, separatedness, pure dimension and relative boundary are retained exactly where

Semivaluations and normalized local boundaries.
  We use v = − log | · |, allow +∞ on the support of a semivaluation, and retain that
  support. For a local ring R and a primary ideal a, a normalized link is a section {v :
  v is centered, v(a) = 1}. Changing a is a radial change with a stated cocycle; it is not

Positivity classes.
  PSH means the speciﬁed plurisubharmonic class in each theory. Classical psh is the upper-
  semicontinuous curve-test notion, with the extended −∞ convention where stated. Real
  PL means the real linear extension of the local integral piecewise-linear class. Semi-
  positivity is its residue/model nefness condition. Locally Fubini–Study is the local ﬁ-
  nite logarithmic-max class with its prescribed denominators. Ordinary CLD smoothness
  uses smooth tropicalizations; weak smoothness permits harmonic tropicalizations. These
  classes are distinct. CLD-v2 denotes the second generated CLD psh stage in the book.

Currents and products.
  d0 d00 = d0 d00 is the CLD Hessian. A continuous function deﬁnes the order-zero current
  [h]. CLD means Chambert–Loir–Ducros; GJR means Gubler–Jell–Rabinoﬀ; BFJ means


                                               4

     Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson. Positivity of one Hessian current does not, by itself, construct
     mixed wedge products or prove classical psh recognition.

Global energy and mass.
  E 1 denotes the ﬁnite-energy class of the named theory. Reference weights, raw intersection
  mass and probability normalization must be ﬁxed before comparing energies or measures.
  Quotienting by R means uniqueness modulo additive constants. Zero top mass cannot be
  divided into a probability measure. The aﬃne-cone probability operator is an explicitly
  separate convention.

Complex singularity data.
         1,1
  α ∈ HBC    (X, R) is a real Bott–Chern class. MP means Mesquita–Piccione, DXZ means
  Darvas–Xia–Zhang, and BJ means Boucksom–Jonsson. I-equivalence records multiplier-
  ideal data; P -equivalence records the ﬁner envelope/singularity data. The latter cannot

Polyhedral normalization.
   PA denotes piecewise-aﬃne functions. BMPS means Botero–Mazzon–Pille-Schneider. Lit-

FULL FAMILY DOSSIER
5     Recognizing continuous zero-Hessian functions
Active items: P06.2. Status: Open in the residual scope.

5.1    Atomic targets
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

5.2    What constitutes a solution
Prove recognition for general continuous zero-Hessian functions in a new stated scope, or
construct a counterexample satisfying the original strict ambient hypotheses. Make scalar-
current ascent and two-sign regularization separate obligations. Ordinary smooth, weakly
smooth and G-local real-PL conclusions have distinct consequences.

5.3    Full statement and detailed state of the art
The supplied singular descent theorem Book Theorem 18.12.1 settles P06.1: classical plurihar-
monicity implies local real PL regularity throughout the original scope, including arbitrary
singular points. P06.2 retains the reverse bridge from a current equation to the curve-test
notion.
Problem 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and let X be a good, separated,
strict, boundaryless K-analytic space. If a continuous h satisﬁes d0 d00 [h] = 0, must h be
classically pluriharmonic, or harmonic under the hypotheses where a classical harmonic notion
is available, outside the positive cases recorded below?
   The residual problem has two logically separate gates. One must ﬁrst control the zero-
current equation after scalar extension, and one must then regularize continuous positive-
current functions into the CLD-psh hierarchy. The next proposition records that these two
gates suﬃce and that every counterexample must obstruct at least one of them.

Proposition 5.1. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that there is an analytic extension L/K such that, for the scalar-extension map π : XL → X
and hL := h ◦ π, the following two conditions hold:
  (1) the current equation ascends, so that d0 d00 [hL ] = 0;

  (2) current positivity regularizes for the two signs of hL : if f ∈ {hL , −hL } and d0 d00 [f ] ≥ 0,
      then f is CLD-psh.
Then h is classically pluriharmonic and locally R-PL. If X is pure-dimensional, then h is also
GJR harmonic.
Corollary 5.2. Let K be complete and nontrivially valued, let X be a good, separated, strict,
boundaryless K-analytic space, and let h : X → R be continuous with d0 d00 [h] = 0. Suppose
that h is not classically pluriharmonic. For every analytic extension L/K, at least one of the
following failures occurs:

                                                 42

 (1) d0 d00 [hL ] 6= 0;

 (2) one of hL and −hL has nonnegative Hessian current but does not belong to the CLD-psh
     hierarchy.

For L = K, the ﬁrst alternative is impossible. Hence every negative answer to P06.2 furnishes,
in one of the two signs of h, a continuous zero-current function outside the CLD-psh hierarchy.
If X is pure-dimensional, this is a counterexample to the converse of Book Proposition 15.9.8
in its stated scope.

    This reduction neither pulls a continuous current through an arbitrary scalar extension
nor proves positive-current regularization. It identiﬁes those operations as distinct proof
obligations and shows that a negative answer to P06.2 produces a zero-current function outside
the CLD-psh hierarchy at the ground ﬁeld. In the pure-dimensional scope this would disprove
the missing nonsmooth converse in Book Proposition 15.9.8.
    The following dated veriﬁcation history explains those positive cases. Its former P06.1
residuals are superseded by the singular descent theorem.
    The real-coeﬃcient  √ convention in the resolved P06.1 theorem is sharp. On the strict
semistable annulus, 2 log |T | is classically pluriharmonic and R-PL but is neither Q-PL nor
integral PL; see Book Proposition M.1.1.

harmonic function on a good strict quasi-smooth analytic space is R-PL and GJR harmonic.
The proof ﬁrst passes, after a ﬁnite ground-ﬁeld extension, to Temkin’s rigid étale cover by

only for the ﬁnite étale aﬃnoid equalizers where its hypotheses hold. The theorem requires
no global quasicompactness, separatedness, or boundarylessness.

a ﬁnite, ﬂat, surjective analytic cover by a neighbourhood in any veriﬁed P06.1 regularity
range, then Book Corollary M.1.1 descends R-PL regularity and GJR harmonicity for every
classically pluriharmonic function. It is an application of the ﬁnite-ﬂat R-PL descent theorem
[GJR26, Proposition 5.11], not a claim that arbitrary singular germs admit a ﬁnite-ﬂat cover
of this kind.
    The published curve comparison also settles every strict analytic curve, including singular
and nonreduced curves [GR25a, §4.1.2 and Proposition 3.15]. At that checkpoint, the residual

## 1. Exact result and its limitations

Write $D=d'd''$ and $t_f=-\log|f|$ for an analytic unit. An ordinary
CLD form is a form locally described by smooth coefficients in unit
moments on **ordinary open** neighbourhoods. All integration uses the
canonical calibration of the actual analytic structure. In particular,
generic Artinian lengths are retained on nonreduced spaces.

**Theorem (finite separable curve transport).** Let $K$ be complete and
nontrivially valued. Let $E/K$ be any finite separable extension, with its
extending absolute value, and let $\pi:X_E\longrightarrow X$ be scalar
projection. Suppose $X$ is good, separated, strict, boundaryless, and
purely one-dimensional, possibly singular and nonreduced. For every
continuous finite $h:X\longrightarrow\mathbb R$,
\[
                D[h]=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                D[h\circ\pi]=0.                       \tag{1}
\]
This applies on every ordinary open subspace. No scalar stability,
regularization, algebraic-model, normality, or product hypothesis on $h$
or $X$ is added. The forward implication is the claimed partial progress;
reverse finite-separable descent is not counted as new.

The new analytic approximation statement used for a finite Galois
extension is the following. For every invariant
$\beta\in A_c^{0,0}(X_E)$ there are $\alpha_j\in A_c^{0,0}(X)$ and one
compact $C\subset X$ such that
\[
 \operatorname{supp}\alpha_j\subset C,\qquad
 \big\|(D(\beta-\pi^*\alpha_j))_{\mathrm{Rad},E}\big\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
                         \longrightarrow0,             \tag{2}
\]
with all errors supported in $\pi^{-1}(C)$. Thus every continuous finite
multiplier has convergent differentiated pairings on this **fixed**
compact support. Approximation is not claimed to be ambient $C^2$
convergence in coefficient-norm coordinates or exact smooth descent.

The theorem is a scalar gate, not a solution of original P06.2. It
proves no recognition on arbitrary ambient germs, no two-sign
positive-current regularization, and no ascent in dimension at least
two or to an infinite or transcendental extension. The original status
is `partial` and `candidate=false`. No prior quadratic draft, catalogue
assertion, native review, or publication receipt is a premise. Every new
supporting lemma is proved below. External analytic foundations are
stated precisely in Section 2 and their uses checked in the proof.

On a pure curve the equation means
\[
 B_h(\psi):=\int_X h\,(D\psi)_{\mathrm{Rad},K}=0
          \quad\text{for every }\psi\in A_c^{0,0}(X).     \tag{3}
\]
A convention-dependent constant sign in current duality has no effect
on vanishing. The differentiated current itself is not assumed to be a
measure. The smooth top forms in (3) do define finite signed Radon
measures on their compact supports.

## 2. Exact analytic dependencies and source checks

CLD refers to Chambert-Loir--Ducros, *Formes différentielles réelles et
courants sur les espaces de Berkovich*, arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025.
GR refers to Gubler--Rabinoff, *Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions
on Berkovich spaces*, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September 2025. Numbering is
that of these cached primary snapshots, whose statements and proof
bodies, not just the former drafts' descriptions, were inspected.

1. **Affinoid foundations.** CLD 11.1.1--2: an affinoid spectrum is
   compact Hausdorff; its algebra is noetherian with closed ideals; the
   map to its prime spectrum is surjective. CLD 11.1.5: every point of
   an affinoid has rational affinoid neighbourhoods inside any prescribed
   ordinary open. CLD 11.1.7--8: a good space has an affinoid
   neighbourhood basis; ordinary opens are analytic domains; analytic
   sections form a sheaf also for ordinary opens, and
